White field; left a grinning cartoon man in a navy blazer, hands on hips; center a smiling red-haired cartoon boy in a white polo dropping a green coin into a green piggy bank beside three rising stacks of green coins; heavy black "HOW THE RICH / RAISE WINNERS" with a curved arrow to the child. respect. So there you have it, 15

script.analysis: All 21,005 stored characters read in two contiguous ranges with canonical hash match. Hook: rich kids' advantage is knowledge, not money; subscribe CTA; "I guarantee some of these will change how you think". Fifteen lessons: how money works; assets vs liabilities (owner-occupied home and car as liabilities; rental income to pay a $2,000 car lease); anti-entitlement and three-generation loss pattern; social skills; earn more vs spend less; habits; money as a tool; long-term thinking; skills over money; money working for you; bigger problems bigger rewards; time value and skeptical view of degrees; good vs bad debt (rental leverage); 80/20 rule and straight-A tradeoffs; money doesn't make you better. Close: best inheritance is knowledge. Generic Rich-Dad-style content without data, studies, stories or worked numbers; repetitive filler. Several overgeneralizations about wealthy families and risk-free framing of leveraged real estate. Heavy fillers ("um", "uh") preserved; not audio-verified.

beat_map.beat: Rich-kid advantage hook, CTA, lessons 1-7: money basics, assets vs liabilities and rental-funded car lease, anti-entitlement/three generations, social skills, earning focus, habits, money as tool
Lessons 8-15: long-term thinking, skills, money working, bigger problems, time and degrees, good vs bad debt, Pareto and grades, humility; knowledge-inheritance close

claim_audit: 0:10500 "Owner-occupied home is a liability" follows a popular Rich Dad definition (cash-flow based), not standard balance-sheet accounting; a home is an asset that also provides imputed rent. "Wealthy people never buy luxuries with their own earned income" is an absolute overgeneralization. Rental properties paying a $2,000/month lease ignore vacancy, maintenance, leverage and tax effects. "First generation builds, second maintains, third loses" is a proverb; widely repeated 70%/90% loss statistics trace to weak consulting surveys - no figures given here, claim unverified.

0:10500 "Limit to cutting expenses, virtually no limit to earning" overstates earning flexibility for most workers; both levers matter. "Poor families stress about $5 coffee while wealthy generate $500/week" is a stereotype, not evidence.

10500:21005 "Overestimate one year, underestimate ten" is an aphorism. Good debt: "tenants essentially pay off the loan" and "banks love good debt because it is less risky" omit vacancy, rate, leverage and concentration risks; investment-property loans typically carry higher rates and stricter terms than owner-occupied mortgages, contrary to the implication. Pareto principle described correctly as a heuristic. "Most wealthy people are humble" unsupported. No tax, statistic or product claims to verify against primary sources.

topic.analysis: Intergenerational financial literacy and wealth mindset: what affluent families supposedly teach. Audience: parents and self-improvers. Very saturated, aspirational topic; this version lacks evidence on parental financial socialization (an existing research field) and offers adult-mindset lists instead.
topic.novelty_and_corpus_angle: Original angle: use actual research on financial socialization (e.g., parental money talk, allowances, custodial accounts) and age-specific exercises with real numbers (custodial Roth for teen earnings, matching savings), separating evidence from proverb.
